tasks.title: The workspaces dock becomes components — DockView / WorkspaceFrame / ColumnGroup / PaneRow, beside its surface
tasks.description:
**Antonio, 2026-08-13:** *"for the sidebar check better but I guess F006/P032 is a good candidate for a refactoring task to align the component to the rules."*

Do it the way the exposé was done (F003/P082/T420) and to the recipe that came out of it: **AGENTS.md § 0b-bis, "How to structure and build a component"**. That section was written from this exact shape of problem and names every step.

# Why this one, and why now

Three bugs in a row in this file during 2026-08-13 were **wiring** bugs, and the suite could not see any of them:

1. `.previous(bool)` read at build time on a tree that deliberately never rebuilds on focus (`chrome_signature` excludes it) — frozen for the session.
2. The mark published for the current workspace only, while the history is written solely for same-workspace moves — so a cross-workspace jump marked nothing.
3. ⚠️ **Still unfixed at the time of writing** — the mark does not appear even after both. See T426; the next step there is a **trace**, not another fix.

None of the three could have survived a headless test of a component, and none of them was catchable by reading. That is the argument for this task, not tidiness.

# The gap against § 0b-bis, measured

`heca/src/providers/workspaces/mod.rs` — **2200 lines**, ~35 composition sites, and:

- **`pane_card()` :739 takes ELEVEN positional arguments** and carries `#[expect(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` whose own note calls it *"phase-local fix before a larger ChromeCx refactor"*. § 0b-bis step 2: properties are struct fields, the constructor is a struct literal.
- **`column_view()` :1051 is a separately written near-duplicate** of the same row shape. § 0b-bis step 1: split by what a piece *owns*, one owner per question.
- **Functions, not components** — nothing in the file can be built in a test, so nothing has a headless test of its own. § 0b-bis steps 4 and 7.
- **Seams threaded one argument at a time** (`emit_intent`, `signals`, `drag`, `ws_state`, `programs`, `theme`) instead of one group. § 0b-bis step 3.
- `providers/workspaces/model.rs` is already the surface's `model.rs` and is **good** — it computes per-entry state (`SidebarItemState::{Active, Visited, None}` :226) from plain data. Keep it; the components read it.

# The shape to build

```
heca/src/chrome/<dock>/            (or providers/workspaces/, if the provider seam must stay)
├── mod.rs           host wiring — the ONLY file touching AppState / ChromeCtx
├── model.rs         EXISTS, keep — the session reduced to entries with their state
├── pane_row.rs      one pane: name, icon, badges, its states, its menu, its drag id
├── column_group.rs  a column: its rows + the MarkerGroup bar
├── workspace_frame.rs  a workspace: the DockFrame, its header, its collapse
└── dock_view.rs     the whole dock: the frames, the cursor
```

⚠️ **The state model is the part to get right, and it is the part that has been wrong.** A row has four simultaneous states — selected, cursor, last-visited, hovered — each with a different update path (build-time vs bound signal). § 0b-bis's rule is that a component owns its own states; the extraction must make it impossible to set one at build time that changes on focus. `pane_active` / `pane_previous` in `ChromeSignals` show the working pattern.

# Behaviours to preserve — every one is load-bearing

Drag source + drop target ids, the `nav_key` as the row's one identity, the context menu declared on the widget, `KeyHint::on_peek` (`row_peek`), the info segments and badges, per-mount cursors, `Visibility`-swapped active/inactive titles, and the collapse set projected post-sync. **Pixel-identical output**: this is a surface Antonio verifies by hand.

# Verification (Antonio drives)

The sidebar looks and behaves exactly as before — and the four row states can be reasoned about one file at a time, with a headless test each.
